tasks.name: Repair corrupted design doc control bytes (e)
tasks.description: docs/plans/2026-09-07-shared-entry-validator-hardening-design.md line 25 has three raw ASCII control bytes (NUL 0x00, 0x1F, 0x7F) inside a regex span where the readable intended text is [\x00-\x1f\x7f]; git flags it binary via the NUL-in-first-8000-bytes heuristic (the file decodes fine; the em-dashes/arrows are valid UTF-8). Fix by a byte-level rb->wb replace of exactly those three control bytes with their escaped ASCII text (b'[\x00-\x1f\x7f]' -> b'[\\x00-\\x1f\\x7f]'); NOT a whole-file rewrite, and do NOT transcribe cat -v's [^@-^_^?] literally. Then run the definitive full commander suite + make test-hooks gate.

steps.description: Confirm the corruption (RED): the file contains a raw NUL byte so git treats it binary. This is a byte-level defect, NOT a UnicodeDecodeError — the file decodes fine today.
steps.expected: 1 (one line contains a raw NUL byte).

steps.description: Byte-level replace the three control bytes with their escaped ASCII text (rb->wb; leave the valid em-dashes/arrows untouched; do NOT whole-file-rewrite; do NOT transcribe cat -v's [^@-^_^?] literally).
steps.command: PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 .venv/bin/python -c "p='/Users/roberthyatt/Code/ironclaude/docs/plans/2026-09-07-shared-entry-validator-hardening-design.md'; b=open(p,'rb').read(); n=b.replace(b'[\x00-\x1f\x7f]', b'[\\x00-\\x1f\\x7f]'); assert n!=b and b'\x00' not in n; open(p,'wb').write(n); print('replaced', len(b), '->', len(n))"
steps.expected: prints 'replaced <M> -> <N>' (exactly one span replaced; no NUL remains); no AssertionError.

steps.description: Verify GREEN: no NUL + literal escaped regex present + content intact.
steps.expected: 1 (the literal escaped regex /[\x00-\x1f\x7f]/.test(entry) is now present). Follow with: PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 .venv/bin/python -c "d=open('/Users/roberthyatt/Code/ironclaude/docs/plans/2026-09-07-shared-entry-validator-hardening-design.md',encoding='utf-8').read(); assert '\x00' not in d and 'isSafeSharedEntry' in d; print('clean', len(d))" -> prints 'clean <N>'.
